source_name: Институт за човекови права (IHR) — quarterly monitoring of the ДКСК
why_relevant: Publishes structured quarterly monitoring of the anti-corruption commission's caseload, including how many procurement-related cases were opened and how they were resolved. Gives an independent completeness check on what ДКСК itself publishes.

source_name: Open Data Macedonia / GetData mirrors of ДКСК datasets
why_relevant: Third-party mirrors that have historically re-published ДКСК registers in machine-readable form. Valuable as a fallback when the institutional site restructures and old URLs break, and as a source of historical snapshots.

source_name: Академија за судии и јавни обвинители — public procurement training materials
why_relevant: Judicial training decks on public procurement explain, in practitioner language, how ДКЖЈН and the Administrative Court actually reason about appeals — evaluation criteria, grounds for annulment, evidentiary standards. Materially improves parsing and classification of decision texts.

source_name: Open Data MK (opendata.mk) — CGK's open-data platform
why_relevant: NGO-run structured re-publication of public-spending data. Hosts the 'Индекс на рационалност' (Rationality Index) — item-level comparisons of what different institutions paid for identical goods/services — plus databases on contracts over EUR 1 million, direct-award contracts and budgets. This is a searchable, category-indexed alternative to the official e-nabavki portal and is far easier to mine for price benchmarks and repeat vendors.

source_name: Јавни набавки на општините (javninabavki.opendata.mk) — municipal procurement database
why_relevant: Dedicated CGK database of municipal public procurement. Search coverage indicates it supports year-on-year spend comparisons and supplier concentration findings (e.g. 'ten firms received 25% of the value of all tenders in 2023'). Municipal-level award data is normally the hardest to assemble from the official portal, so this is a high-value structured layer.

Third-party re-publication of MK contracting data in a normalised, cross-country schema, with search and analytics over tenders and awards. Because it standardises national portal data plus TED, it is the fastest route to structured award records, buyer/supplier aggregates and single-bidding indicators without scraping e-nabavki directly.

source_name: OCP Data Registry — North Macedonia: OpenTender publication record
why_relevant: Registry entry describing the MK open-contracting dataset: what is published, in what format (OCDS JSON/Excel/CSV), the source portal it derives from, and coverage/quality caveats. The canonical starting point for locating and validating any machine-readable MK procurement dataset, and a pointer to further publications.

EU-supported Western Balkans civil-society coalition on procurement anti-corruption, active since 2012, with CGK as the North Macedonia member. Carries a country page and a documents library (national and comparative), which gives regional benchmarking of MK procurement practice and points to the CSO actors doing the monitoring in each country.

CGK's Active Transparency Index scores how much mandatory information institutions actually publish — including procurement plans, contracts and realised contracts. Useful as a meta-source: it tells you which contracting authorities publish reliably (so their data can be trusted/collected) and which are opaque, which shapes collection strategy for the whole A2 workstream.

OCCRP-affiliated investigative newsroom (founded 2017) focused on corruption, crime and governance, explicitly including government spending and procurement. Notable for building its own tooling to search public databases, so its stories often surface contract-level and beneficial-ownership detail that never appears in a tender notice. Bilingual mk/en output.

BIRN Macedonia's investigative platform (BIRN Macedonia founded 2004, part of the regional Balkan Investigative Reporting Network). Publishes investigations, analyses and reports on matters of public interest, with a track record on public money and contracts. BIRN's regional network also means MK procurement stories get cross-linked into Balkan-wide datasets and reporting.

source_name: Платформа на граѓански организации за борба против корупцијата (antikorupcija.mk)
why_relevant: Umbrella platform networking MK civil-society organisations on anti-corruption, with an explicit member directory and an archive of positions/reactions. Public procurement is named as a priority area. Primarily valuable as an actor-map pointer: the members list enumerates the CSOs worth tracking individually for procurement monitoring.

TI national chapter, formed December 2006, working on good-governance and anti-corruption policy. Relevant to A2 as a producer of procurement-related policy analysis and as an operator of citizen corruption-reporting channels that occasionally surface tender complaints. Note the .org.mk domain appears to be the chapter site; treat the exact hostname as unverified.

Citizen corruption-reporting channel run jointly by Transparency International – Macedonia and the Center for International Relations (email, web app, phone, hashtag #korupcijaMK). Reported cases sometimes concern tender procedures and give early, ground-level signals that never enter the official portal. Low structure, high noise — treat as a lead generator, not a dataset.

source_name: Open Government Partnership — North Macedonia country page and commitments
why_relevant: OGP tracks MK's procurement-transparency commitments (web publication of procurements MK0146, beneficial-ownership transparency in procurement MK0144, earlier MK0073, public disclosure of beneficial owners MK0185) together with Independent Reporting Mechanism assessments and civil-society comment. This is the best single map of what procurement data is supposed to become available, when, and who is contesting the gaps — plus bilingual mk/en action-plan PDFs.

source_name: ПОВ Портал / ovp.gov.mk — national OGP portal, procurement-as-open-data commitment
why_relevant: The Macedonian-language national Open Government portal where procurement-as-open-data commitments are drafted with civil-society input. The commitment text explains precisely why external monitoring by media and CSOs has been hard (manual data collection) and documents the Public Procurement Bureau's fix — one-click bulk download of the 'Concluded Contracts' module. That is the key operational detail for planning A2 collection.

source_name: Open Society Foundations Western Balkans — policy brief: Open Data and Public Procurement in North Macedonia
why_relevant: Donor/CSO policy brief (2025) assessing the actual state of open procurement data in MK — notes that after an initial wave of disclosures following Bureau recommendations, access to procurement data and spending remains limited. Gives an independent, dated quality assessment of the official data layer, which is essential for calibrating how much to trust e-nabavki-derived datasets.

source_name: Отворени финансии (open.finance.gov.mk) — Ministry of Finance transaction portal
why_relevant: Official but aggregator-style: publishes public-sector payment transactions (reported at over 12.5 million records) in near real time, searchable by paying institution and by supplier. Complements award notices with actual payments — you can check whether a company supplies several public entities and how much it earns from each, which is the cleanest available vendor-concentration signal. Sits adjacent to this cell because CSOs and media use it as their analysis substrate.

News agency run by the Metamorphosis Foundation, a long-standing digital-rights and transparency CSO. Covers open-data and public-spending transparency developments in Macedonian (e.g. coverage of the Otvoreni Finansii portal launch). Useful as an ongoing announcement channel for changes in procurement data availability, and as a bridge to Metamorphosis's own transparency research.

source_subtype: news outlet (secondary re-publisher of CSO analysis)
why_relevant: Macedonian outlet that reliably picks up and amplifies CGK procurement-monitoring findings (e.g. the report that 71% of the value of emergency procurements went to five firms). Acts as a fast, searchable secondary index of CSO procurement analysis in Macedonian, often naming the firms involved.

National news agency that carries CGK procurement findings verbatim (e.g. 'every third public procurement contract was concluded in a procedure with only one bidder'). Provides a dated, quotable mk-language record of CSO monitoring output and is easier to search historically than some NGO sites.

Donor programme directory of Macedonian civil-society organisations with per-organisation profile pages (CGK and Transparency International – Macedonia both appear). Useful purely as an actor-map expander: it enumerates funded CSOs, their thematic focus and contact/web details, which is how you find the smaller local procurement watchdogs that never rank in search.

Regional CSO anti-corruption network assessment covering Macedonia, using the Corruption Monitoring System methodology, with quantified procurement observations (e.g. centralised procurement rising to 11% of total analysed procurement value from 4% in 2011). Provides methodology and longitudinal baselines that a purely news-driven view lacks.
